title: Well-specified bug: double debit on transfer retry
tests: Baseline. A complete, well-written bug with a clear root cause, an open PR and a customer remediation action. A capable model should score near 100; the traps check it does not overstate progress or widen the scope.

tickets.summary: Transfer retry after timeout debits the source account twice
description: Customer transferred $250 from their cheque account to savings on mobile web. The spinner hung for about 30 seconds and then showed "Request timed out (ERR_TXN_504)". They tapped Retry.
Result: the cheque account was debited $250 twice, and savings was credited once.
1. Log in on mobile web and start a transfer between two own accounts.
2. Add more than 30s of latency between the API and the database (we used toxiproxy).
Expected: one debit and one credit.
Three customers have reported this so far (support calls on 5, 6 and 8 September).

comments.author: Priya Nair
body: 1. The Retry button calls POST /api/transaction/transfer again with no idempotency key, so the server treats it as a new transfer.
2. The debit and the credit are not in one database transaction, so when the credit times out the first debit stays committed.

comments.author: Tom Becker
body: Confirmed on 3.1.4 staging with Priya's steps. It does NOT reproduce on desktop web: desktop disables the submit button and has no Retry button after a timeout.

comments.author: Aroha Walker
body: Finance will need to reverse the duplicate debits for the three affected customers manually. Marcus, can you raise that with Finance Ops?

comments.author: Priya Nair
body: PR #218 is open: wraps the debit and credit in a single transaction and adds Idempotency-Key header support to the transfer endpoint. Waiting on code review.

answer_key.expect: Retrying a transfer after the ERR_TXN_504 timeout debits the source account twice while crediting the destination only once.
The bug affects version 3.1.4 and the fix is targeted at 3.2.0, which releases on 2026-09-24.
Root cause (per Priya's reproduction): the retry resends the transfer with no idempotency key, and the debit and credit are not in a single database transaction.
The ticket is In Progress, assigned to Priya Nair, and the fix (PR #218) is waiting on code review.
Three customers are affected and need their duplicate debits reversed manually by Finance; Marcus Reid was asked to raise this with Finance Ops.
The ticket does not confirm that the Finance reversal request has been raised or that the three customers have been refunded.
Next actions include getting PR #218 reviewed and merged, and confirming the customer reversals with Finance Ops.
Claims PR #218 has been merged, or that the fix is deployed or released.
answer_key.claim: PR #218 has been merged and the fix is already deployed to production.

answer_key.expect: Claims desktop web is also affected (QA confirmed it does not reproduce on desktop).
answer_key.claim: The double debit affects desktop web as well as mobile web.
